title: agent-bridge message envelope, version 1
description: One message between agents on the bridge, as docs/PROTOCOL.md defines it: what a board row is when it leaves the board (`bridge-board read --json`) and what any other transport must deliver. `body` is the message; `headers` and `citations` are derived from it and must agree with it (bridgelib.protocol.check verifies that, the schema cannot).

v.description: Envelope version. An additive change keeps 1; a change that makes a valid v1 envelope invalid bumps it.

topic.description: The thread this message belongs to. Reserved prefixes: conv:, panel:, live:, dm:, room:, fix: (see PROTOCOL.md §7).

seq.description: Position in the topic, 1-based, assigned by the transport, never reused inside an open topic.

author.description: Who posted it — an identity the transport resolved, never one the author claimed (PROTOCOL.md §2).

kind.description: What the message does in the exchange (PROTOCOL.md §5). task and system are the transport's own bookkeeping.

to.description: Whom it is for: null or * = everyone in the topic; @<role> = the members holding that role; an identity; a bare family name (claude, cursor, copilot, codex) on a request = a turn for a peer that is not running.

reply_to.description: seq of the message this one answers, in the same topic. An answer/done/blocked that replies to a request closes it when it comes from the request's owner or requester.

created_at.description: Unix time (seconds) the transport accepted the message.

body.description: The message text: optional header lines (`key: value`, up to the first blank or non-header line), then free text. Markdown is allowed; a code fence is not an answer (PROTOCOL.md §4, §8).

headers.description: Derived: the header lines of body, keys lower-cased. Known keys are listed; others are allowed and carried as strings.

shape.description: request: what the answer must look like; tokens a script checks: table, file:line, json, diff, patch, decision, command.

missing.description: blocked: what the author lacks, and the default it will take if nobody answers. `-`, `none`, `n/a` do not count.

card.description: A card to the human: decision (a choice only they own) or fact (information nobody else has).

dir.description: turn: the workspace the dispatched run starts in (stored resolved).

mode.description: turn: the run's mode; write needs dir.

owner.description: Informational: the identity the requester expects to answer.

citations.description: Derived: every `path.ext:line[-end]` the body cites, in order, each once — the evidence the file:line rule is judged on. Resolution against a workspace is not part of the envelope.

identity.description: user:<name> | <family>@primary | <family>#<pid> | <family>:task<N> | <family>@live:<peer> | <family>@hop | board | a script slug. No whitespace, no `+`, not starting with @ or *, never a bare `user:`.

role_ref.description: @<role>: leader, member, observer, or a persona slug such as root-cause.
